content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "When you tell the incoming caregiver what still needs doing, is that information communicated verbally, written down, or recorded somewhere like an app or shared document?", "answer": "Caregiver notes are shared via a family handover log and a family messaging app. The outgoing caregiver shares relevant notes with the incoming caregiver, so the information is recorded rather than purely verbal."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "How do you determine which tasks still need to be done at handover time — do you work from a checklist, review a log of what was completed during the day, or rely on memory?", "answer": "The outgoing caregiver compiles an unfinished task list, drawing on the family handover log and an evening task checklist. Task completion is manually recorded, so the list reflects what has and has not been checked off during the day."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "Can you describe the specific steps involved in getting things ready for the next day — for example, does this include preparing medications, laying out equipment, or scheduling anything?", "answer": "The partner reviews the next-day schedule, then prepares the items needed for the next day, and marks completed preparation tasks in the checklist. The specific physical items prepared are not specified in the available information."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "Does this evening handover and preparation routine happen every day, or only on certain days, and does the content of the routine change depending on the day?", "answer": "The routine occurs each evening when care responsibility changes in the household. Whether content varies by day of the week is not specified, though the next-day schedule is reviewed each time, implying content can differ based on upcoming needs."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "What happens if the person taking over in the evening is unavailable or significantly delayed — is there a backup plan or does the current caregiver continue until they arrive?", "answer": "Incoming caregiver unavailability is listed as a recognised exception. The specific backup plan is not specified, but unresolved tasks are left open and the relevant task owner is contacted when items cannot be confirmed."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "Is there any existing tool, app, or written record used during the day to track what care tasks have been completed, or is that tracking done entirely from memory?", "answer": "Task completion is manually recorded in the family handover log and the evening task checklist. Only participating caregivers can read the shared log. There is no automated tracking; recording is done by hand by the caregivers themselves."}]}
